title: Deep dive: redeem a limited code without overselling
caption: Read-then-write lets two checkouts take the last use; one conditional update makes the database decide.

messages.label: SELECT uses → 9 999
messages.note: Code LAUNCH10K has a limit of 10 000. Checkout 1 sees one use left.

messages.label: SELECT uses → 9 999
messages.note: Checkout 2 reads before checkout 1 writes: it also sees one left.

messages.label: SET uses = 10 000
messages.note: Checkout 2 does too: 10 001 discounts given, and the counter says 10 000. The lost update grows with traffic.

scenarios.name: Fix: conditional update
scenarios.summary: One statement checks and increments: UPDATE … SET uses = uses + 1 WHERE id = ? AND uses < limit. Rows affected tells you the answer.

messages.label: UPDATE … WHERE uses < limit
messages.note: Checkout 1's update runs first and takes the row lock.

messages.label: 1 row → apply
messages.note: uses is now 10 000: the last use.

messages.label: UPDATE … WHERE uses < limit
messages.note: Checkout 2's update runs after the lock is released.

messages.label: 0 rows → used up
messages.note: The condition fails: checkout 2 shows "code fully redeemed". No oversell is possible.

scenarios.name: Payment fails after redeem
scenarios.summary: A use taken by an order that never completes must come back: redeem inside the order transaction, or reserve with a TTL and release on failure.

messages.label: payment declined
messages.note: The order fails after the use was counted.

messages.label: release (uses − 1)
messages.note: If the release is lost, the code runs out early. Mitigation: reservation rows with a 10-minute TTL and a sweeper.

messages.label: UPDATE uses + 1
messages.note: With the reservation expired, the use is available again.

scenarios.name: Alternative: token pool
scenarios.summary: For a doorbuster, pre-issue 10 000 tokens into an in-memory list and pop one per redeem: no hot row lock, but you must reconcile tokens lost to crashes.

messages.label: LPOP LAUNCH10K
messages.note: One atomic pop per redeem: ~100k ops/s on one cache node.

messages.label: token 7 312
messages.note: Checkout 1 owns that use; the order row records the token.

messages.label: empty → used up
messages.note: The pool is empty: rejected without touching the database.
